rows.description: A child with a calm resting face is neither happy nor sad. A neutral face is not a sign of anger or disinterest, and adults avoid over-reading it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, sadness, anger, interest

rows.description: A child holds in laughter in class or waits for a turn, using self-control. Restraint is a growing skill, and children need chances to release energy afterward.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: amusement

rows.description: A school-age child after a long day or illness looks drained, moves slowly and snaps easily. Weariness needs rest and low demands, and lasting exhaustion calls for checking sleep, health and stress.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: tiredness

rows.subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
rows.description: A child who goes pale may be scared, ill, faint, shocked or cold. Sudden paleness with dizziness needs sitting down, water and adult help.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: fear, surprise

rows.subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
rows.description: A school-age child sweats from heat, exercise, nervousness before a test or illness. The cause cannot be told from the sweat alone, so setting and other signs matter.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anxiety

rows.description: A child learns idioms, hints and jokes, and asks what someone meant. Indirect speech may show politeness or humour, and asking what someone means is a good habit.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: amusement
related concepts: humour

rows.description: A child says cheese and smiles for a photo but looks tired in a candid moment. A posed smile shows cooperation, not necessarily feeling, and both kinds of image tell different stories.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: tiredness

rows.description: A child begins to notice small changes such as a slight frown or lower voice in a parent. Subtle signals are easy to miss or over-read, so a short check keeps them honest.

rows.description: A child keeps a straight face at a surprise, waiting for the right moment or to avoid teasing. The child still feels the excitement, and adults may enjoy the delay.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: excitement, surprise

rows.description: A school-age child says okay through tight lips when a rule feels unfair. Politeness shows learned self-control, yet the anger still needs a safe outlet afterwards.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anger, trust
